posts.title: [Software] BricksChat: Generate buildable MOCs from your own parts and download instructions
posts.text: Hi everyone, I built BricksChat and released it this week, it is an app which is like GPT, but for designing MOCs. I tried hard to avoid the "AI slop" problem and developed it in a way to generate actually valid buildable designs in 3D (including source .ldr/.mpd files and pdf instructions) from real parts. Moreover it also checks them against existing and official sets or MOCs in the catalogue for originality (including parts and subassemblies) to disclose a percentage of how much of it was copied (and the AI can be steered to attempt full originality and prevent copying from any existing sets). Or you can prompt it to copy explicitly to so a modification of your existing build, alt-build or combination of multiple sets. You can write a prompt like "design a set looking like this castle", attach an image and even specify a parts list (or sets you already own) to let it design what you can actually build from what you have at home right now. It is still an early prototype, but I was surprised how well it worked compared to what I've seen AI producing before. I wanted to share it here with you to give it a try. Web: https://brickschat.com/ What is currently on my backlog: Improving instruction generation (both pdf and interactive instructions) – I am not yet happy with the current quality and want to improve it ASAP. In case of big builds its not reliable at all. Proficiency in build techniques – Btw its already quite good incl. SNOTs, Technic mechanisms etc. But still not close in quality to human designed sets Improving speed & performance. Possibility to order the parts needed. Mobile app Let me know what other features would you like to prioritize! And share a link or photo of what you have built with it. For full transparency, this is my project and it has both free access and paid options: so far its very resource intensive, so I will see if it can pay to at least cover its own server bill. Thanks! Mirek PS: It is potentially very good at routing users to human designed MOCs (it always checks if anything with the similar topic already exists). If you are a creator, here is a waitlist https://brickschat.com/creators PS2: Is anyone interested in how it actually works from the AI side & github and so? It is not yet released & I am gauging the interest https://github.com/brickschat-com/brickschat-harness

posts.title: DC Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Said this on here before but the format in and of itself is a one trick pony gimmick that really only works with the MCU because it's what started the trend and the Monsterverse is so loosely connected it doesn't matter. You can drop into any of those films no context. The MCU itself is trying a Gunn half reboot thing because even their Cinematic Universe isn't stable. This format is NOT a money printer. It worked once recently as a gimmick and people got tired of that gimmick and now only show up if Spider-Man or nostalgia characters are leading a project. Well a big part too is they're so insular. How are you supposed to jump on when everything expects you to have either seen 3 other things at minimum or know the origin of the characters from other franchises. People talk about how people treat Raimi Spider-Man, for example, as the source material but every follow up rushes or doesn't do the foundational stuff because they just expect you to have seen those films. Like after Tom leaves, probably in a bit under a decade they're gonna get Miles in to replace him. That Miles actor, even if they only do one trilogy then bounce will be in the role for a bit under a decade too. By the time they next potentially would do a fresh jumping on point basic Spider-Man story the Raimi films may well be pushing 40 years old! Now Spider-Man is big enough to survive this, everyone sees Spider-Man stuff, even the old ones. But what chance do characters like the Hulk or Green Lantern stand there?

posts.title: DC Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Correct. They’re not going to leave the big names on the shelves. But if Man of Tomorrow bombs, they’re not going to consider anyone but Batman or his villains to be a big name. Justice League bombing was enough to keep Superman off screen for nearly a decade. Man of Tomorrow bombing would be another nail in his coffin. Green Lantern went over a decade and the best he could get was a tv show where he spent about five minutes actually using his ring. As much as all of us here might want to see more of these characters, executives aren’t going to green light projects unless they think they’ll be successful. And DC as an IP hasn’t been strong enough to carry itself for close to a decade. I think the bigger issue is that superheroes and comic books aren’t as popular with the younger generation as they were with the generation that grew up with the MCU. Part of that is probably because the older generation was so into them that they made it uncool for the next generation. But, as you say, it also doesn’t help that Marvel hasn’t been putting out much in terms of good content.

posts.title: Lego Blockly: Graphical Common Programming Environment Web App (Using Intuitive Blockly) for All Lego Robotic Platforms.
posts.text: The ESP32 PF Bridge uses the IRremoteESP8266 library which encore the 16 bits to PF timings including the addition of start and stop specially timed bits. This is also because I use this library that I can use other 38 khz remote protocol... But I believe the library "IRsend" can also be used for Unmodulated signals. Anyway, I asked AI Claude to modifiy the ESP32 PF IR Bridge and Claude did differently making its own timing. So I added a LegoPFIR_BLE_ESP_WROOM_32_V4.ino in the project. ( https://github.com/BlissCA/lego-blockly/tree/dev/SketchArduino ) Please have a look to the following code at the beginning of the arduino code to define your RF Send GPIO pin and also the RF_INVERT might be necessary, I don't know... // ------------------------------------------------------ // RF OOK TX (unmodulated LEGO PF bit stream) // ------------------------------------------------------ #define RF_SEND_PIN 17 // Set to 0 to disable the RF output completely #define RF_TX_ENABLED 1 // Set to 1 if your RF TX module needs inverted logic // (normally: GPIO HIGH = carrier ON = "mark") #define RF_INVERT 0 // Set to 1 to protect the RF timing from interrupts on this core // (the burst lasts ~16 ms). posts.title: Lego Blockly: Graphical Common Programming Environment Web App (Using Intuitive Blockly) for All Lego Robotic Platforms.
posts.text: Thank you for even considering my inquiry, Yves. I apologize for not making my inquiry clearer! OK, all I am looking for is the bit stream that is emitted at GPIO 4 - but without the 38kHz modulation. Instead of having a 38kHz PF "on-bit", I just would like to get the plain "bit on/off" signal. And I would then feed this signal into the input of my 433MHz transmitters. OOK (on/off keying) is the simplest way of sending a signal to a receiver: Input bit = 1 -> send a 433MHz carrier signal, just that. There is no information stored in this signal; it is just "there". Bit = 0: Send nothing. The matching receiver (these are old LINX TX/RX modules) turns its output on, when it detects a 433MHz carrier signal, and keeps it off when there is nothing. This is the same with the TSOP modules: When they see a 38kHz IR signal, they turn their output on, when there is nothing, it remains off. So using these RF TX/RX modules, I don't need the 38kHz modulation of an on-bit, I just need the on-bit itself and feed that into the transmitter. That will modulate the on-bit (as 433MHz) signal. GPIO 4 sends on = 38kHz (on/off) signals; I would like to have a second GPIO output that just sends on = on. Does that make any sense? Best Thorsten

posts.title: DC Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: I don't think it's all that complicated- I feel like there's a simple flow of "I don't like the current universe's direction - I don't think it'd be easy to fix - I would like them to start again." 1. I don't like the current universe- I haven't liked a single DCU project (at least from the ones I've seen, and I doubt creature commandos or supergirl will sway me). They range from "ok but with some major lore changes I dislike" (superman 2025) to "I would say it feels like the writers hated the character, but it's not just how it feels, the writers have actively said some crazy stuff about the character" (Lanterns). 2. It wouldn't be easy to fix. There are some things that aren't all that major- Kal-El's family being evil is a ridiculous change but probably wouldn't have much of an impact on future stories- but others, like what they did to Hal (and John tbh) require a lot of work to get back into a good position- Hal's situation is pretty much unfixable without a truckload of retcons. Not to mention the main issues- the weird sort of semi-break from the DCEU and the resulting random (and mostly R-rated) selection of projects. When this all started Gunn said something along the lines of the reason it's not starting with Batman and Wonder Woman is because he goes with the best scripts, but... if the projects we've gotten were better scripts than anything anyone's brought him on any of the major heroes, I feel like you're having some troubles in the writing phase. Even if you announced batman, wonder woman, flash, etc movies today, it's too late. Too much of the universe has been established. 3. Feasibility of starting again. Yes, there's an ownership transfer- which means a lot of projects in early development are getting paused or cancelled. This very much works in favor of starting a new universe, and would help avoid the weird unclean "I'm gonna keep my friends as the same characters" partial reboot of the DCEU into the DCU. In addition, the DCU is in a rough state. Sure, the MCU had Hulk underperform, but Supergirl did worse than morbius. Not to mention the slew of low-viewership and/or heavily controversial R-rated projects. If I was an exec looking at this, I'd say the smart move is to pause everything in production until MoT comes out. If it does great, awesome, greenlight batman and wonder woman. If it doesn't... dig up that schedule they spoke about when the DCEU was first collapsing that was a 5-year plan focused on the trinity. I don't think that's necessarily the case. Paramount isn't the lego group, and studios are always going to want to make a cinematic universe out of anything they can. They're not going to leave the big names on the shelves because Supergirl bombed.

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Depends if the first wave of sets is considered too spoiler filled. I think even if a delay happened they'd still shove out a trailer in Q3 2027. I feel even if the material was a good quality, we're 39/40 films deep, makes the most sense to have the focal characters being the popular ones or from recent films because those are what the audience may recall. I really hope we get some of the potential cameo characters in 2027 spoilery Doomsday sets and that we don't need to wait until late 2028/2029 to get them. The current rumour is that they won't even start filming Avengers: Secret Wars until February 2027. Sure they can work on some entirely VFX shots in the meantime, but I think the best option would be to just shift Avengers: Secret Wars back to May 2028, releasing on the 20th anniversary of the MCU. At which point all the Phase 7 projects are delayed a year. They'd want to capitalise on viewings, so why not split Avengers: Secret Wars into two movies also? May 2028 and December 2028 respectively, having a runtime of around 2 hours 25 minutes each, for a combined 4 hours 50 minutes rather than a 3 hours 45 minute Avengers: Secret Wars as is the current speculation. They definitely have a large enough cast where they can pad out the runtime to a split. I think there's also an underlying notion that fans want a bigger conclusion and having a three film finale to wrap up 20 years of the MCU with two of those films releasing in the 20th anniversary year would definitely spark conversation and interest. The rumours are: 67019 - $60 (October 1st) 67020 - $120 (October 1st) 67021 - $160 (October 1st) It's possible they were simply labelled as 'Avengers' and a leaker attached them to Secret Wars because of the release date. These could be the Avengers: Doomsday spoiler sets just releasing in October 2027 Alternatively the Avengers: Doomsday spoiler sets are just being kept under a lot of secrecy, but it is admittedly strange that we have some claims that certain characters are featured. They probably should have released it in 2025 alongside the Fantastic Four movie which would have improved sales from people buying it for Galactus. I'd have thrown in another trophy figure - Thor on the Leviathan. In terms of microfig core Avengers we are missing Thor, Black Widow and Hulk. Hulk can probably be represented as a brick but would be nice to get Thor & Black Widow.

posts.title: 11388 Venetian Neighbourhood
posts.text: It's possible (architectural trademarks do exist, though usually more for more recent construction). But it's probably just be a matter of wanting a condensed scene with lots of variety, since real buildings often tend to be much larger and more repetitive than Lego ones (hence why Architecture sets based on real buildings don't typically aim for minifigure scale). And in historic cities like Venice, buildings are often clustered with buildings that have a similar architectural style (with you having to travel farther to get a sense of the variety of architectural styles the city has to offer). So even a large scene like this one would probably make for a less varied and interesting build if they focused on recreating specific buildings realistically, instead of doing a more generalized layout like this.

posts.title: BrickCode Studio NQC and NXC IDE for Apple Silicon and Linux
posts.text: Sounds interesting! Just throwing that in: The Scout can do that natively as well. It sends out the VLL commands on fwd/on rev when you turn on output C (=VLL LED) fwd/rev. This works with the Mindstorms IR remote as well: Press C fwd/rev, and the Scout will turn on its VLL LED and send the VLL codes out. The Scout can also send all VLL codes using the command (copied from the Scout SDK manual): Opcode ‘vll’ Sends a 7-bit VLL command out over the VLL output vll source, number Legal range for ‘source’: 0 (variable) and 2 (constant value). No need for an USB tower, nor a control program ;) Best Thorsten
